summary: The note describes Citizen Advisory Boards (CABs) in the city of Riverfork, which city officials implemented in a more focused way on September 5, 2023 and Mayor Elaine Costas re-envisioned after her November 7, 2023 re-election. It covers how the boards are structured, the best practices behind them, praise and criticism from residents, and the East Riverfork housing project as a success story. It closes with a call for residents to take part and notes that Brookdale plans similar boards.
one_line: Riverfork's Citizen Advisory Boards, relaunched in 2023, boost citizen participation in local governance, with notable successes, some criticisms, and a call for residents to get involved.
key_facts: Riverfork city officials implemented Citizen Advisory Boards (CABs) in a more focused way on September 5, 2023.
Mayor Elaine Costas re-envisioned the purpose of CABs after her landslide re-election on November 7, 2023.
Each Riverfork CAB consists of 12 appointed residents serving staggered two-year terms.
Riverfork CABs cover areas including Transportation, Public Safety, Economic Development, and Parks and Recreation.
CABs meet bi-monthly and draft recommendations that go to the city council or relevant municipal departments.
Applications for CAB membership have soared since the revitalization.
James Clarkson, a retiree on the Public Safety Advisory Board who has lived in Riverfork over 40 years, said he can now directly shape safety initiatives affecting his grandchildren.
Riverfork's four best practices are clear objectives, inclusive recruitment, professional facilitation, and transparent processes (public release of minutes and recommendations).
Andrea Holmes, a high school teacher on the Education Advisory Board, said the boards sparked 'a tangible increase in public trust'.
Local business owner Derek Thompson argues the boards offer the illusion of influence because ultimate decisionmaking power stays with the city council.
Some board recommendations have been postponed or diluted due to budgetary constraints or competing interests.
The CAB for Housing and Urban Development drafted an affordable housing plan for East Riverfork that was swiftly approved and received additional funding through community fundraisers.
Mayor Brendan Sullivan of nearby Brookdale announced plans to institute similar boards.
